takeaway: Iliopsoas is formed by psoas major and iliacus, passes deep to the inguinal ligament, attaches to the lesser trochanter and flexes the thigh at the hip.

question.text: Which of the following statements regarding the iliopsoas muscle is correct?

answer.text: It passes deep to the inguinal ligament.

lines.text: Psoas major and iliacus merge to form iliopsoas, not psoas minor.
It passes deep to the inguinal ligament, under this rope bridge, on its way to the thigh.
It attaches to the lesser trochanter of the femur, not the greater trochanter.
It is the main flexor of the thigh at the hip joint, so it does not extend it.
Psoas major is supplied by the anterior rami of L1 to L3, not the superior gluteal nerve.
lines.say: Psoas major is supplied by the anterior rami of L one to L three, not the superior gluteal nerve.

lines.text: So the correct statement is that it passes deep to the inguinal ligament.
